headline: New law assigns Interstate 27 route numbers to future interstate sections of the Ports-to-Plains Corridor in Texas and New Mexico.
what_it_does: The law names the future interstate highway parts of the Ports-to-Plains Corridor in Texas and New Mexico as Interstate 27 (I-27). Between Sterling City and Lamesa, Texas, the route splits: U.S. Route 87 becomes I-27E, and Texas Routes 158 and 349 (by way of I-20) become I-27W. One section, U.S. Route 287 from Dumas, Texas, to the Oklahoma border, is instead numbered I-127N.

who_it_affects.group: Drivers and truckers who travel these routes in Texas and New Mexico
who_it_affects.how: Roads they use will carry new interstate route numbers once those sections become part of the interstate system.

who_it_affects.group: Texas and New Mexico state transportation agencies
who_it_affects.how: They will use the new I-27, I-27E, I-27W, and I-127N numbers for these corridor sections.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed into law March 22, 2024. The summary does not give a separate start date, and the numbers apply to corridor sections as they become part of the interstate system.
